summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis report (card N6) proposing a pre-registered rodent working-memory (WM) experiment to test whether Azure B (methylene blue's demethyl metabolite) fails to match parent methylene blue (MB) on a WM task, despite Azure B's stronger MAO-A inhibitory potency in vitro. The document is a hypothesis/assay-proposal at TRL 1–2: no new experiments have been run, and the key behavioral comparison (Azure B vs. MB on the same WM task) is explicitly classified as UNKNOWN. It synthesizes existing literature on MAO-A IC50 values and MB cognitive effects to frame a mechanistic assumption-kill experiment.

content_blocks.title: Document Metadata and Policy
content_blocks.content: Public report from Mol Labs, dated 2026-09-25. Policy: PUBLIC_REPORT_ONLY. STATUS_LABEL: NEGATIVE. Risk class: research-discussion. Polarity: negative. Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Related prior: N5 (not proof of Azure B WM failure). Kill cost tier: 1. Time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: redox-vs-MAO. Vault hold: no. Note: Identical science to openlabs.md; no sequence, analog list, or unpublished construct; no mol_ keys.

content_blocks.title: Central Claim (Hypothesis N6)
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered rodent working-memory task, Azure B alone fails to match parent methylene blue — WM Δ ≤70% of MB (or outside a pre-registered MB-equivalence band) — despite Azure B's stronger MAO-A potency under identical enzyme conditions. This is a PREDICTION; the experiment has NOT been run.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale and Mechanism
content_blocks.content: Redox-vs-MAO assumption-kill: if WM tracks MAO-A potency, Azure B (≥6× stronger MAO-A than MB in vitro) should match or exceed MB; if WM tracks parent redox/structure, Azure B underperforms on the same WM task. Azure B is MB's demethyl metabolite and a high-potency reversible MAO-A inhibitor (IC50 ≈11 nM vs MB ≈70 nM under identical conditions). MB is a potent reversible MAO-A inhibitor. Low-dose MB improves discrimination/metabolic memory. Redox-disabled N-acetyl MB loses mitochondrial ET/neuroprotection (not a declared WM endpoint). Competing caveat: PK/brain exposure may make Azure B underperform without killing the MAO story.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Evidence
content_blocks.content:
1. PMID 22197611 / DOI 10.1016/j.taap.2011.12.005 (Petzer 2012): Azure B MAO-A IC50 ≈11 nM vs MB ≈70 nM under identical conditions (~6× more potent). Status: LITERATURE (confirmed).
2. PMID 17721552 / DOI 10.1038/sj.bjp.0707430 / PMC2078225 (Ramsay 2007): MB is a potent reversible MAO-A inhibitor; serotonin-toxicity prediction. Status: LITERATURE (confirmed).
3. PMID 17428524 / PMC2040387 (Gonzalez-Lima class): Low-dose MB improves discrimination learning/metabolic memory with COX framing — no Azure B arm. Status: LITERATURE (confirmed, no Azure B comparator).
4. PMID 21454572 / DOI 10.1074/jbc.M110.208447 / PMC3091255 (Wen 2011): MB alternative electron transfer; N-acetyl-MB (redox-dead) loses mitochondrial complex activity/OCR/neuroprotection — not a WM endpoint. Status: LITERATURE (confirmed, not WM).

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat N5 as proving N6 — N5 asked selective MAO-A-i ≠ MB and listed Azure B as confound; it did not measure Azure B vs MB on WM.
2. MAO IC50 ≠ brain WM PD — Petzer is enzyme inhibition without a cognition endpoint.
3. PK/brain exposure — Azure B could underperform from distribution, not mechanism; soft-complete empty ≠ negative result.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: Hypothesis is refuted if: On the pre-registered WM task, Azure B alone matches parent MB within the MB-equivalence band (WM Δ >70% of MB or inside band) — especially under exposure/occupancy-matched conditions — so MAO-potency/metabolite-sufficiency for WM survives.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay / Execution Plan
content_blocks.content: Method: propose-assay. Execution status: NOT_RUN. Proposed design: Pre-registered delayed alternation or Gonzalez-Lima-style discrimination task in rodents; Azure B alone vs parent MB (± optional selective MAO-A-i arm); with occupancy/exposure readout. Pre-specified α/N required. Do not invent observed Δ or dosing. Time to refute: 4 weeks. Kill cost tier: 1 (low cost).

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis
content_blocks.content:
Three critical ablations identified:
1. Remove same-task WM contrast of Azure B alone vs parent MB: Without the behavioral head-to-head, stronger MAO-A LITERATURE and MB memory LITERATURE cannot show Azure B fails to match MB on WM.
2. Remove stronger-MAO-A/MAO-comparable framing (Azure B vs MB enzyme potency anchor): Without the potency contrast, underperformance is just 'Azure B weak,' not an assumption-kill of MAOI-explains-WM.
3. Remove N5≠proof + soft-complete-empty≠failure + PK-competing discipline: Treating N5 or empty PubMed as already deciding Azure B WM failure would invent a negative result left UNKNOWN.

key_findings: Hypothesis N6 is a PREDICTION/proposed assay — no new experiments have been run (execution_status=NOT_RUN).
Azure B (MB demethyl metabolite) has ~6× stronger MAO-A inhibitory potency than MB in vitro: IC50 ≈11 nM vs ≈70 nM (Petzer 2012, PMID 22197611).
MB is a potent reversible MAO-A inhibitor with serotonin-toxicity implications (Ramsay 2007, PMID 17721552).
Low-dose MB improves rodent discrimination learning/metabolic memory (Gonzalez-Lima class, PMID 17428524), but no Azure B arm exists in this literature.
The key behavioral comparison — Azure B alone vs. MB on the same WM task — is explicitly classified as UNKNOWN (soft-complete = 0).
The central mechanistic question is whether WM benefit tracks MAO-A potency (favoring Azure B) or parent redox/structure (favoring MB), which cannot be resolved without the proposed experiment.
N5 (prior hypothesis card) does not prove N6: N5 tested selective MAO-A-i ≠ MB but did not run Azure B vs MB on WM.
PK/brain exposure is a competing explanation: Azure B could underperform due to distribution, not mechanism.
Redox-dead N-acetyl-MB loses mitochondrial ET/neuroprotection (Wen 2011, PMID 21454572), but this is not a WM endpoint.
Kill cost tier = 1 (low); estimated time to refute = 4 weeks; FTO status = UNKNOWN.
